objects.original: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces E,F,G, continuous linear maps A:E->G and B:F->G, and independent standard Gaussian inputs X,Y.
objects.reconstructed: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel spaces E,F,G, continuous real-linear maps A,B, and the product of their standard Gaussian measures.
objects.evidence: The output map is exactly (x,y)->Ax+By. Independent measurable Gaussian random vectors have joint law gamma_E prod gamma_F; conversely the coordinate projections of that product realize the source inputs. No Gaussian input or map is substituted.

domains.original: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces with their Borel sigma algebras; singular maps and zero dimensions permitted.
domains.reconstructed: NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace for each of E,F,G.
domains.evidence: A finite-dimensional real inner-product space is complete and second-countable, so the inferred completeness and characteristic-function uniqueness hypotheses are not extra mathematical assumptions. BorelSpace fixes exactly the source sigma algebra. There is no positive-dimension, rank or invertibility binder. The focused test instantiates F=EuclideanSpace R (Fin 0), B=0 and A=id.

quantifiers.original: For arbitrary E,F,G and A,B, balance holds for every t in G; every pair of independent standard Gaussian inputs then has the asserted law.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally quantified space/typeclass parameters and A,B; hbalance universally quantifies t:G; conclusion is equality of the transformed product law.
quantifiers.evidence: The universal t binder is unchanged, not restricted to a basis or almost everywhere. Passing from arbitrary independent realizations to their joint distribution removes no law-level quantifier: pushforward depends only on the joint law. No existential choice of maps or covariance is introduced.

assumptions.original: Continuous linearity; finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel structure; independent actual standard Gaussian laws; complementary adjoint squared norms.
assumptions.reconstructed: A:E->L[R]G and B:F->L[R]G; the listed structural classes; the actual product stdGaussian measure; forall t, ||A.adjoint t||^2+||B.adjoint t||^2=||t||^2.
assumptions.evidence: Measure.prod encodes genuine independence, not merely Gaussian marginals. stdGaussian is the pinned coordinate-independent standard Gaussian law. Continuous linearity gives measurability; its adjoint is the Hilbert adjoint. Probability/finite/SFinite instances come from stdGaussian, with no extra integrability, density, invertibility, lower-bound or positive-definiteness premise.

conclusion.original: AX+BY has exactly standard Gaussian law in G.
conclusion.reconstructed: ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian F)).map (fun p=>A p.1+B p.2)=stdGaussian G.
conclusion.evidence: Equality of Borel probability measures is the complete vector-law assertion, not only equal covariance, coordinate marginals, approximate distance or an IsGaussian predicate. The map is exactly the source sum.

scopes.original: Generic exact law for independent Gaussians under complementary linear maps, including singular/zero-dimensional cases.
scopes.reconstructed: The same unconditional law-level theorem, with the application balance supplied as an explicit hypothesis.
scopes.evidence: No conditional-on-parent independence, seed execution, physical-query equality, recursive error or query bound is asserted. The module and exposition explicitly reserve concrete source adapters and deterministic translation for later work. Finite-dimensional zero spaces remain valid singleton vector spaces.

constant_dependencies.original: Standard centered unit-covariance Gaussian; no application scale, dimension-dependent constant or error tolerance.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: stdGaussian in all spaces and exact balance; characteristic exponents -norm^2/2.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Pinned charFun_stdGaussian and charFunDual_stdGaussian use exp(-norm^2/2). The proof preserves this factor and derives equality without slack. D_s,v,r,m,d occur only in the planned application exposition, not in the theorem binders or conclusion.
